query: Why do some agents have longer resolution times?

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: The query is explicitly ABOUT agents, but this column merely restates the existing 'assigned_to'/'closed_by' original columns, adding no new analytical axis. Values are grounded (agent names present in table), but it is trivially redundant.

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorising the short_description into incident type gives a genuine axis to compare which issue types (and thus which agents' workloads) drive longer resolution times. Values map soundly from the descriptions (database, VPN->connectivity, application). Some overlap with original 'category' column slightly reduces usefulness.

per_column.name: problem_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual_device vs facility_wide) is a plausibly useful complexity axis for resolution time. However groundedness is weak: 374 rows labelled 'infrastructure' and specific scopes like 'facility_wide'/'department' are not derivable from terse descriptions like 'VPN issue' — these appear to be confident inventions where the text is silent.

per_column.name: incident_complexity_signal
per_column.rationale: A complexity flag is directly relevant to why resolution times differ, but it is a bare boolean offering limited leverage, and the true/false assignment is not clearly warranted by the short one-line descriptions, suggesting speculative labelling.

per_column.name: agent_closure_alignment
per_column.rationale: Whether the assigned agent matches the closer could relate to handoffs affecting time, so it has some leverage. But this is derivable directly from comparing existing 'assigned_to' and 'closed_by' columns (partly redundant), and the boolean labelling is only partially verifiable from the samples shown.

judge.rationale: The set offers a couple of genuinely useful axes (incident_category, and to a lesser degree problem_scope and complexity) for explaining resolution-time differences. However 'assigned_agent' is a trivial restatement of existing columns, and several boolean/scope columns provide thin leverage. Groundedness is mixed: category is well-read from descriptions, but problem_scope and complexity assert specifics (facility_wide, department, complexity booleans) not supported by the terse source text, indicating some hallucination.
